hypothesis: A batch-level accepted-liquid contract that includes upstream mass, upgrading, capital recovery and separately allocated R&D lock-up interest will expose cost/yield bottlenecks hidden by raw bio-oil yield alone.

interface.evidence_rule: calculated output is always MODEL_ONLY; no input label can promote it automatically

cross_lane_edges.interface: separate plant capital recovery and R&D principal/lock-up interest
unique stream IDs and net incremental-cost coproduct credits
accepted liquid MJ and lifecycle cost may later enter energy-supply scenarios; no phone-compression claim
sparse coherent data access remains an algorithmic resource bound, not readable classical memory

literature.source: Dimitriadis, Tuler and Bezergianni, ACS Omega

open_gaps: No traceable Pangola batch mass/energy closure
No catalyst lifetime, hydrogen or utility-energy dataset
No verified coproduct market or commercial financing terms
falsifier: Reject any accepted-fuel cost claim if the product fails the frozen acceptance specification, the mass balance misses its preregistered tolerance, upgrading inputs are omitted, cost/provenance fields are unknown, or coproduct streams overlap.
next_gate: Run independent, provenance-pinned Pangola batch trials and compare HTL/pyrolysis only under the same accepted-product and lifecycle-cost boundary; in parallel, Lane A must independently implement parity mapping/decoding and compare matched small graph workloads under the merged QAOA contract.
